name: Web Application Security
description: Recognizing and mitigating common web vulnerabilities such as injection, XSS, CSRF and broken access control.

questions.question: Using parameterized queries (prepared statements) is the primary defense against which vulnerability?
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries send user input as data separate from the SQL command, so it can never change the query's structure.

questions.question: What happens in a cross-site scripting (XSS) attack?
options: Attacker-controlled script is executed in other users' browsers in the context of the vulnerable site
The attacker floods the server with requests until it crashes
The attacker guesses a user's password by trying many combinations
Database queries are modified to return extra rows
questions.explanation: XSS occurs when untrusted input is rendered as executable script in a page, letting it run with the site's privileges in a victim's browser.

questions.question: Which cookie attribute prevents client-side JavaScript from reading a session cookie?
questions.explanation: HttpOnly hides the cookie from document.cookie, limiting session theft via XSS. Secure only restricts it to HTTPS.

questions.question: Which is the most effective mitigation for cross-site request forgery (CSRF) on state-changing form submissions?
options: Requiring an unpredictable anti-CSRF token per session or request, combined with SameSite cookies
Using GET requests for all state-changing actions
questions.explanation: A secret token the attacker's site cannot read, together with SameSite cookie restrictions, ensures forged cross-site requests are rejected.

questions.question: A logged-in user changes the URL /invoices/1001 to /invoices/1002 and sees another customer's invoice. Which OWASP Top 10 category does this fall under?
questions.explanation: This is an insecure direct object reference (IDOR): the server fails to check that the user is authorized for the requested object, which is Broken Access Control.

questions.question: What is the main security purpose of a Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header?
options: To encrypt all traffic between browser and server
To prevent SQL injection in backend queries
To compress page content for faster delivery
To restrict which sources scripts and other resources may load from, reducing the impact of XSS
questions.explanation: CSP tells the browser which origins are allowed to supply scripts, styles and other content, blocking injected inline or third-party scripts.

practical.title: Fix a vulnerable database query
practical.instructions: This login lookup is vulnerable: query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '" + email + "'"; db.execute(query). Name the vulnerability class, then rewrite the code (any language or library) so it is safe, and add one sentence explaining why your fix works.
practical.expected_output: Identifies SQL injection and rewrites using a parameterized query/prepared statement with a placeholder (?, $1, %s, :email) and the email passed as a separate parameter, explaining that input is treated as data, not SQL. Example: db.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?", (email,)).

rubric.hint: Concatenating user input into SQL creates a SQL injection vulnerability.
Replace the concatenated value with a placeholder such as ?, $1, %s or :email.

rubric.description: Passes the value as a separate parameter
rubric.hint: Pass the email as a separate argument to execute/query or bind it to the prepared statement.
Explain that the database treats parameters as data, never as part of the SQL command.

tasks.title: Study the OWASP Top 10
tasks.description: Read the current OWASP Top 10 and, for each category, write a one-line description and one example. Note the primary mitigation for each.
tasks.completion_criteria: A table of all ten categories with an example and a mitigation for each.

tasks.title: Complete introductory Web Security Academy labs
tasks.description: Create a free PortSwigger account and complete the apprentice-level labs on SQL injection and cross-site scripting in their intentionally vulnerable lab environment. Record the root cause and fix for each lab.
tasks.completion_criteria: At least four apprentice labs solved with notes on root cause and remediation.

tasks.title: Harden HTTP headers and cookies
tasks.description: On an app you built, add a Content-Security-Policy, set session cookies with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite, and add anti-CSRF protection to forms. Verify with browser developer tools.
tasks.completion_criteria: Response headers and cookie attributes shown in dev tools, and a forged cross-site form submission is rejected.

tasks.title: Perform a secure code review of your own app
tasks.description: Review a full-stack project you own against the OWASP Cheat Sheet Series for authentication, access control, input validation and output encoding. Fix the issues you find and document them.
tasks.completion_criteria: A findings report with at least five reviewed areas, severity ratings, and commits fixing the identified issues.
